Jbob:

Been wondering if Microsoft uses A.I. for any aspect of WoW?

As for Microsoft using AI for any aspect of WoW? … Probably, yeah.
I’d argue for rather simple things though, like tying up loose ends, reviewing mistakes and stuff like that.

If you could use AI to scan for and correct stuff like N-gons in deforming meshes within development and some variances here & there to save time for developers — It’d allow for better quality work on modeling and the time they’re dispensed for the players to enjoy

The prime issue I’d argue – is the overreliance of it and not overviewing its use – to see if it was used properly. AI isn’t always correct, nor does it always achieve the desired result.

posts.name: Orlando11
posts.cooked:
Jbob:

Been wondering if Microsoft uses A.I. for any aspect of WoW?

It depends on what you mean by A.I. People have been putting some type of “intelligence” into computer programs since 1842 when Ada Lovelace wrote “Note G” to describe how someone could use Charles Babbage’s Analytical Engine to calculate Bernoulli numbers.

Recently a new technique for “intelligence” has come along where computers use a bottom up approach to problem solving rather than a programmer using a top down approach but A.I. has been around in some form for quite some time with “expert systems” being a good example.
